claim: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is an aggressive interstitial lung disease associated with progressive and irreversible deterioration of respiratory functions that lacks curative therapies.
source: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is an aggressive interstitial lung disease associated with progressive and irreversible deterioration of respiratory functions that lacks curative therapies.
evidence: This is a general characterization of IPF based on established medical knowledge about the disease.

claim: The P2RX7/IL18/IFNG axis is downregulated in IPF patients.
source: Transcriptomic analyses show that the P2RX7/IL18/IFNG axis is downregulated in IPF patients and that P2RX7 has immunoregulatory functions.
evidence: The claim is supported by transcriptomic analyses presented in the manuscript.

claim: P2RX7 has immunoregulatory functions.
source: Transcriptomic analyses show that the P2RX7/IL18/IFNG axis is downregulated in IPF patients and that P2RX7 has immunoregulatory functions.
evidence: The claim is supported by transcriptomic analyses presented in the manuscript.

claim: Activation of the P2RX7/IL-18 axis in immune cells limits lung fibrosis progression in a mouse model.
source: Using our positive modulator of P2RX7, we show that activation of the P2RX7/IL-18 axis in immune cells limits lung fibrosis progression in a mouse model by favoring an antifibrotic immune environment, with notably an enhanced IL-18-dependent IFN-γ production by lung T cells leading to a decreased production of IL-17 and TGFβ.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data using HEI3090 in a mouse model.

claim: Activation of the P2RX7/IL-18 axis favors an antifibrotic immune environment.
source: Using our positive modulator of P2RX7, we show that activation of the P2RX7/IL-18 axis in immune cells limits lung fibrosis progression in a mouse model by favoring an antifibrotic immune environment, with notably an enhanced IL-18-dependent IFN-γ production by lung T cells leading to a decreased production of IL-17 and TGFβ.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing changes in immune cell populations and cytokine production.

claim: Activation of the P2RX7/IL-18 axis enhances IL-18-dependent IFN-γ production by lung T cells.
source: Using our positive modulator of P2RX7, we show that activation of the P2RX7/IL-18 axis in immune cells limits lung fibrosis progression in a mouse model by favoring an antifibrotic immune environment, with notably an enhanced IL-18-dependent IFN-γ production by lung T cells leading to a decreased production of IL-17 and TGFβ.
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data showing increased IFN-γ production by T cells.

claim: Enhanced IFN-γ production by lung T cells leads to decreased production of IL-17 and TGFβ.
source: Using our positive modulator of P2RX7, we show that activation of the P2RX7/IL-18 axis in immune cells limits lung fibrosis progression in a mouse model by favoring an antifibrotic immune environment, with notably an enhanced IL-18-dependent IFN-γ production by lung T cells leading to a decreased production of IL-17 and TGFβ.
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data showing decreased IL-17 and TGFβ production.

claim: Pirfenidone and nintedanib have been FDA approved for the treatment of IPF since 2014.
source: Pirfenidone and nintedanib have been FDA approved for the treatment of IPF since 2014.
evidence: This is a factual statement about FDA approval dates that is common knowledge in the field.

claim: Pirfenidone targets the key fibrotic cytokine TGFβ.
source: They target, respectively, the key fibrotic cytokine TGFβ and several receptor tyrosine kinases, thereby affecting fibroblast activation and extracellular matrix protein production (Heukels et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Heukels et al., 2019.

claim: Nintedanib targets several receptor tyrosine kinases.
source: They target, respectively, the key fibrotic cytokine TGFβ and several receptor tyrosine kinases, thereby affecting fibroblast activation and extracellular matrix protein production (Heukels et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Heukels et al., 2019.

claim: Pirfenidone and nintedanib affect fibroblast activation and extracellular matrix protein production.
source: They target, respectively, the key fibrotic cytokine TGFβ and several receptor tyrosine kinases, thereby affecting fibroblast activation and extracellular matrix protein production (Heukels et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Heukels et al., 2019.

claim: Pirfenidone and nintedanib only slow down the progression of IPF.
source: However, they only slow down the progression of the disease, so new therapeutic strategies and targets are needed.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about the limitations of current IPF therapies.

claim: Fibrosis is associated with inflammation.
source: Fibrosis is also associated with inflammation.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about the relationship between fibrosis and inflammation.

claim: Fibrosis is a process of excessive wound healing and tissue remodeling due to repeated epithelial injuries.
source: In fact, fibrosis is a process of excessive wound healing and tissue remodeling due to repeated epithelial injuries releasing damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) that trigger both the adaptive and innate immune systems.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about the pathophysiology of fibrosis.

claim: Repeated epithelial injuries release damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) that trigger both the adaptive and innate immune systems.
source: In fact, fibrosis is a process of excessive wound healing and tissue remodeling due to repeated epithelial injuries releasing damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) that trigger both the adaptive and innate immune systems.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about the role of DAMPs in immune activation.

claim: High levels of extracellular ATP are found in IPF patients.
source: Extracellular adenosine triphosphate (eATP) is a DAMP, released in high concentrations from injured cells in IPF patients (Riteau et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Riteau et al., 2010.

claim: Extracellular ATP is a DAMP.
source: Extracellular adenosine triphosphate (eATP) is a DAMP, released in high concentrations from injured cells in IPF patients (Riteau et al., 2010).
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about the role of ATP as a danger signal.

claim: High levels of eATP are recognized by the P2X7 receptor (P2RX7).
source: High levels of eATP are recognized by the P2X7 receptor (P2RX7) and P2RX7 participates in the establishment of the bleomycin (BLM) lung fibrosis mouse model (Riteau et al., 2010).
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about P2RX7 function and a citation to Riteau et al., 2010.

claim: P2RX7 participates in the establishment of the bleomycin (BLM) lung fibrosis mouse model.
source: High levels of eATP are recognized by the P2X7 receptor (P2RX7) and P2RX7 participates in the establishment of the bleomycin (BLM) lung fibrosis mouse model (Riteau et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Riteau et al., 2010.

claim: Extracellular activation of P2RX7 by ATP leads to conformational rearrangements allowing influx of Ca2+ and Na+ ions into and the efflux of K+ ions from the cell.
source: Extracellular activation of P2RX7 by ATP (Surprenant et al., 1996) leads to conformational rearrangements allowing influx of Ca2+ and Na+ ions into and the efflux of K+ ions from the cell (Karasawa et al., 2017) and to the formation of a large pore mediating macrophage cell death.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Surprenant et al., 1996 and Karasawa et al., 2017.

claim: Extracellular activation of P2RX7 by ATP leads to the formation of a large pore mediating macrophage cell death.
source: Extracellular activation of P2RX7 by ATP (Surprenant et al., 1996) leads to conformational rearrangements allowing influx of Ca2+ and Na+ ions into and the efflux of K+ ions from the cell (Karasawa et al., 2017) and to the formation of a large pore mediating macrophage cell death.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Surprenant et al., 1996 and Karasawa et al., 2017.

claim: The macropore function is intrinsic to P2RX7 and does not involve progressive pore dilatation.
source: The nature of this large pore was subjected to controverse until the recent discovery that the macropore function is intrinsic to P2RX7 and does not involve progressive pore dilatation (Harkat et al., 2017; Pippel et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Harkat et al., 2017 and Pippel et al., 2017.

claim: P2RX7 has the ability to activate the NLRP3 inflammasome.
source: Another feature of P2RX7 is its ability to activate the NLRP3 inflammasome, an event linked to potassium efflux (Di et al., 2018; Muñoz-Planillo et al., 2013), which requires both P2RX7 and TWIK2 activation (Di et al., 2018) and leads to the release of mature IL-1β and IL-18 (Perregaux et al., 2000), through gasdermin D pores.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Di et al., 2018, Muñoz-Planillo et al., 2013, and Perregaux et al., 2000.

claim: NLRP3 inflammasome activation is linked to potassium efflux.
source: Another feature of P2RX7 is its ability to activate the NLRP3 inflammasome, an event linked to potassium efflux (Di et al., 2018; Muñoz-Planillo et al., 2013), which requires both P2RX7 and TWIK2 activation (Di et al., 2018) and leads to the release of mature IL-1β and IL-18 (Perregaux et al., 2000), through gasdermin D pores.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Di et al., 2018 and Muñoz-Planillo et al., 2013.

claim: NLRP3 inflammasome activation requires both P2RX7 and TWIK2 activation.
source: Another feature of P2RX7 is its ability to activate the NLRP3 inflammasome, an event linked to potassium efflux (Di et al., 2018; Muñoz-Planillo et al., 2013), which requires both P2RX7 and TWIK2 activation (Di et al., 2018) and leads to the release of mature IL-1β and IL-18 (Perregaux et al., 2000), through gasdermin D pores.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Di et al., 2018.

claim: NLRP3 inflammasome activation leads to the release of mature IL-1β and IL-18 through gasdermin D pores.
source: Another feature of P2RX7 is its ability to activate the NLRP3 inflammasome, an event linked to potassium efflux (Di et al., 2018; Muñoz-Planillo et al., 2013), which requires both P2RX7 and TWIK2 activation (Di et al., 2018) and leads to the release of mature IL-1β and IL-18 (Perregaux et al., 2000), through gasdermin D pores.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Perregaux et al., 2000.

claim: P2RX7 has the ability to trigger an immune response.
source: Consequently, P2RX7 has the ability to trigger an immune response (Janho Dit Hreich et al., 2023).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Janho Dit Hreich et al., 2023.

claim: IL-1β is a pro-inflammatory cytokine with high profibrotic properties.
source: IL-1β is a pro-inflammatory cytokine with high profibrotic properties, as it promotes collagen deposition through IL-17A and TGFβ production (Doerner and Zuraw, 2009; Sutton et al., 2009; Wilson et al., 2010) but also promotes the activation and recruitment of inflammatory cells such as eosinophils and neutrophils.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Doerner and Zuraw, 2009; Sutton et al., 2009; Wilson et al., 2010.

claim: IL-1β promotes collagen deposition through IL-17A and TGFβ production.
source: IL-1β is a pro-inflammatory cytokine with high profibrotic properties, as it promotes collagen deposition through IL-17A and TGFβ production (Doerner and Zuraw, 2009; Sutton et al., 2009; Wilson et al., 2010) but also promotes the activation and recruitment of inflammatory cells such as eosinophils and neutrophils.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Doerner and Zuraw, 2009; Sutton et al., 2009; Wilson et al., 2010.

claim: IL-1β promotes the activation and recruitment of inflammatory cells such as eosinophils and neutrophils.
source: IL-1β is a pro-inflammatory cytokine with high profibrotic properties, as it promotes collagen deposition through IL-17A and TGFβ production (Doerner and Zuraw, 2009; Sutton et al., 2009; Wilson et al., 2010) but also promotes the activation and recruitment of inflammatory cells such as eosinophils and neutrophils.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about IL-1β function.

claim: Deficiency of IL-1βR or its blockade ameliorate experimental fibrosis.
source: Indeed, deficiency of IL-1βR or its blockade ameliorate experimental fibrosis (Couillin et al., 2009; Gasse et al., 2009; Gasse et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Couillin et al., 2009; Gasse et al., 2009; Gasse et al., 2007.

claim: The role of IL-18 in fibrosis is not clear.
source: In contrast, the role of IL-18 is not clear.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge in the field.

claim: Conflicting experimental studies show that IL-18 could either promote or attenuate fibrosis.
source: Indeed, conflicting experimental studies show that IL-18 could either promote (Zhang et al., 2019) or attenuate (Nakatani-Okuda et al., 2005) fibrosis.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Zhang et al., 2019 and Nakatani-Okuda et al., 2005.

claim: High levels of IL-18BP are associated with reduced overall survival in IPF patients.
source: However, high levels of IL-18BP, a natural antagonist of IL-18, are associated with reduced overall survival in IPF patients (Nakanishi et al., 2021), suggesting that the activity of IL-18 may be required for improved survival or alternatively that high levels of IL-18 are accompanied by more IL-18BP, which leads to poorer outcomes.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Nakanishi et al., 2021.

claim: IL-18 was originally described as IFN-γ-inducing factor (IGIF).
source: IL-18 was originally described as IFN-γ-inducing factor (IGIF) and therefore boosts IFN-γ production by T cells and natural killer (NK) cells (Okamura et al., 1995).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Okamura et al., 1995.

claim: IL-18 boosts IFN-γ production by T cells and natural killer (NK) cells.
source: IL-18 was originally described as IFN-γ-inducing factor (IGIF) and therefore boosts IFN-γ production by T cells and natural killer (NK) cells (Okamura et al., 1995).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Okamura et al., 1995.

claim: IFN-γ has antiproliferative properties.
source: Not only has IFN-γ antiproliferative properties (Elias et al., 1987) but it also inhibits TGFβ activity (Ulloa et al., 1999; Varga et al., 1990) and therefore inhibits fibroblast activation and differentiation into myofibroblasts, alleviates TGFβ-mediated immunosuppression, inhibits extracellular matrix accumulation and collagen production (Duncan and Berman, 1985; Gillery et al., 1992; Gurujeyalakshmi and Giri, 1995; Yuan et al., 1999) and thus promotes an antifibrotic immune microenvironment, making IFN-γ a cytokine with antifibrotic properties.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Elias et al., 1987.

claim: IFN-γ inhibits TGFβ activity.
source: Not only has IFN-γ antiproliferative properties (Elias et al., 1987) but it also inhibits TGFβ activity (Ulloa et al., 1999; Varga et al., 1990) and therefore inhibits fibroblast activation and differentiation into myofibroblasts, alleviates TGFβ-mediated immunosuppression, inhibits extracellular matrix accumulation and collagen production (Duncan and Berman, 1985; Gillery et al., 1992; Gurujeyalakshmi and Giri, 1995; Yuan et al., 1999) and thus promotes an antifibrotic immune microenvironment, making IFN-γ a cytokine with antifibrotic properties.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Ulloa et al., 1999 and Varga et al., 1990.

claim: IFN-γ inhibits fibroblast activation and differentiation into myofibroblasts.
source: Not only has IFN-γ antiproliferative properties (Elias et al., 1987) but it also inhibits TGFβ activity (Ulloa et al., 1999; Varga et al., 1990) and therefore inhibits fibroblast activation and differentiation into myofibroblasts, alleviates TGFβ-mediated immunosuppression, inhibits extracellular matrix accumulation and collagen production (Duncan and Berman, 1985; Gillery et al., 1992; Gurujeyalakshmi and Giri, 1995; Yuan et al., 1999) and thus promotes an antifibrotic immune microenvironment, making IFN-γ a cytokine with antifibrotic properties.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Duncan and Berman, 1985; Gillery et al., 1992; Gurujeyalakshmi and Giri, 1995; Yuan et al., 1999.

claim: IFN-γ alleviates TGFβ-mediated immunosuppression.
source: Not only has IFN-γ antiproliferative properties (Elias et al., 1987) but it also inhibits TGFβ activity (Ulloa et al., 1999; Varga et al., 1990) and therefore inhibits fibroblast activation and differentiation into myofibroblasts, alleviates TGFβ-mediated immunosuppression, inhibits extracellular matrix accumulation and collagen production (Duncan and Berman, 1985; Gillery et al., 1992; Gurujeyalakshmi and Giri, 1995; Yuan et al., 1999) and thus promotes an antifibrotic immune microenvironment, making IFN-γ a cytokine with antifibrotic properties.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Duncan and Berman, 1985; Gillery et al., 1992; Gurujeyalakshmi and Giri, 1995; Yuan et al., 1999.

claim: IFN-γ inhibits extracellular matrix accumulation and collagen production.
source: Not only has IFN-γ antiproliferative properties (Elias et al., 1987) but it also inhibits TGFβ activity (Ulloa et al., 1999; Varga et al., 1990) and therefore inhibits fibroblast activation and differentiation into myofibroblasts, alleviates TGFβ-mediated immunosuppression, inhibits extracellular matrix accumulation and collagen production (Duncan and Berman, 1985; Gillery et al., 1992; Gurujeyalakshmi and Giri, 1995; Yuan et al., 1999) and thus promotes an antifibrotic immune microenvironment, making IFN-γ a cytokine with antifibrotic properties.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Duncan and Berman, 1985; Gillery et al., 1992; Gurujeyalakshmi and Giri, 1995; Yuan et al., 1999.

claim: IFN-γ promotes an antifibrotic immune microenvironment.
source: Not only has IFN-γ antiproliferative properties (Elias et al., 1987) but it also inhibits TGFβ activity (Ulloa et al., 1999; Varga et al., 1990) and therefore inhibits fibroblast activation and differentiation into myofibroblasts, alleviates TGFβ-mediated immunosuppression, inhibits extracellular matrix accumulation and collagen production (Duncan and Berman, 1985; Gillery et al., 1992; Gurujeyalakshmi and Giri, 1995; Yuan et al., 1999) and thus promotes an antifibrotic immune microenvironment, making IFN-γ a cytokine with antifibrotic properties.
evidence: This is inferred from the multiple antifibrotic effects of IFN-γ described.

claim: Parenteral systemic administration of IFN-γ failed in clinical trials.
source: However, parenteral systemic administration of IFN-γ failed in clinical trials (INSPIRE; NCT 00075998) (King and Jobling, 2009), whereas local administration by inhalation showed promising results (Diaz et al., 2012; Fusiak et al., 2015; Prior and Haslam, 1992; Skaria et al., 2015; Smaldone, 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to King and Jobling, 2009.

claim: Local administration of IFN-γ by inhalation showed promising results.
source: However, parenteral systemic administration of IFN-γ failed in clinical trials (INSPIRE; NCT 00075998) (King and Jobling, 2009), whereas local administration by inhalation showed promising results (Diaz et al., 2012; Fusiak et al., 2015; Prior and Haslam, 1992; Skaria et al., 2015; Smaldone, 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Diaz et al., 2012; Fusiak et al., 2015; Prior and Haslam, 1992; Skaria et al., 2015; Smaldone, 2018.

claim: The polarization of T lymphocytes impacts fibroblasts' fate and immune infiltrate.
source: One way to increase IFN-γ production locally and selectively in the lung would be to alter the phenotype of T cells since the polarization of T lymphocytes has been shown to impact fibroblasts' fate and immune infiltrate (Luzina et al., 2008; Shenderov et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Luzina et al., 2008 and Shenderov et al., 2021.

claim: T cells selectively kill myofibroblasts through IFN-γ release and limit the progression of lung and liver fibrosis in preclinical models.
source: Indeed, T cells have been recently shown to selectively kill myofibroblasts through IFN-γ release and limit the progression of lung and liver fibrosis in preclinical models (Sobecki et al., 2022) and set up an immune memory in the long term since IFN-γ-producing tissue resident memory T cells protect against fibrosis progression (Collins et al., 2016), highlighting the importance IFN-γ-producing T cells in this disease.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Sobecki et al., 2022.

claim: IFN-γ-producing tissue resident memory T cells protect against fibrosis progression.
source: Indeed, T cells have been recently shown to selectively kill myofibroblasts through IFN-γ release and limit the progression of lung and liver fibrosis in preclinical models (Sobecki et al., 2022) and set up an immune memory in the long term since IFN-γ-producing tissue resident memory T cells protect against fibrosis progression (Collins et al., 2016), highlighting the importance IFN-γ-producing T cells in this disease.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Collins et al., 2016.

claim: CD4+-producing IFN-γ T cells are decreased in IPF.
source: Accordingly, CD4+-producing IFN-γ T cells are decreased in IPF and correlate with a better prognosis in IPF patients (Giri et al., 1986; Luzina et al., 2008; Xu et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Giri et al., 1986; Luzina et al., 2008; Xu et al., 2006.

claim: CD4+-producing IFN-γ T cells correlate with a better prognosis in IPF patients.
source: Accordingly, CD4+-producing IFN-γ T cells are decreased in IPF and correlate with a better prognosis in IPF patients (Giri et al., 1986; Luzina et al., 2008; Xu et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Giri et al., 1986; Luzina et al., 2008; Xu et al., 2006.

claim: HEI3090 enhances the channel activity and large pore opening of P2RX7.
source: To implement this strategy, we utilized HEI3090, a chemical compound developed in our laboratory. HEI3090 has been previously reported to enhance the channel activity and large pore opening of P2RX7 and also to increase IL-18 levels (but not IL-1β) upon activation of the P2RX7/NLRP3 pathway (Douguet et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Douguet et al., 2021.

claim: HEI3090 increases IL-18 levels (but not IL-1β) upon activation of the P2RX7/NLRP3 pathway.
source: To implement this strategy, we utilized HEI3090, a chemical compound developed in our laboratory. HEI3090 has been previously reported to enhance the channel activity and large pore opening of P2RX7 and also to increase IL-18 levels (but not IL-1β) upon activation of the P2RX7/NLRP3 pathway (Douguet et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Douguet et al., 2021.

claim: The mRNA expression of P2RX7 is downregulated in IPF patients.
source: We found that the mRNA expression of P2RX7 is downregulated in IPF patients (Figure 1A, B), as well as the components of the NLRP3 inflammasome (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1A and 1B.

claim: The components of the NLRP3 inflammasome are downregulated in IPF patients.
source: We found that the mRNA expression of P2RX7 is downregulated in IPF patients (Figure 1A, B), as well as the components of the NLRP3 inflammasome (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: IL-18 is constitutively expressed.
source: Since IL-18 is constitutively expressed (Puren et al., 1999), which partly explains the lack of difference between control and IPF patients (Figure 1B), we investigated the signaling pathway downstream of IL-18.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Puren et al., 1999.

claim: IL18R1, IL18RAP, and IFNG are downregulated in IPF patients.
source: We showed that IL18R1, IL18RAP, and IFNG (Figure 1B) are downregulated in IPF patients.
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The expression of P2RX7 correlates with the IFNG response in IPF patients.
source: Indeed, we showed that the expression of P2RX7 and IL18 signaling (IL18 and IL18RAP) correlates with the IFNG response as well as with immunoregulatory interactions required for changing the phenotype of T cells (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The expression of IL18 signaling (IL18 and IL18RAP) correlates with the IFNG response in IPF patients.
source: Indeed, we showed that the expression of P2RX7 and IL18 signaling (IL18 and IL18RAP) correlates with the IFNG response as well as with immunoregulatory interactions required for changing the phenotype of T cells (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The expression of P2RX7 and IL18 signaling correlates with immunoregulatory interactions required for changing the phenotype of T cells in IPF patients.
source: Indeed, we showed that the expression of P2RX7 and IL18 signaling (IL18 and IL18RAP) correlates with the IFNG response as well as with immunoregulatory interactions required for changing the phenotype of T cells (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Activation of P2RX7 with HEI3090 in mice 7 days after BLM administration reduced the development of pulmonary fibrosis.
source: Activation of P2RX7 with HEI3090 in mice 7 days after BLM administration reduced the development of pulmonary fibrosis, as evidenced by less thickening of alveolar walls and free air space (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by histological data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Fibrosis is reduced by 40% in lungs of HEI-treated mice.
source: This quantification showed that fibrosis is reduced by 40% in lungs of HEI-treated mice.
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification of the Ashcroft score.

claim: The percentage of CD140a (PDGFRα)-positive cells in non-immune cells subset is reduced in lungs of HEI3090-treated mice.
source: We showed that both the percentage of CD140a (PDGFRα)-positive cells in non-immune cells subset (Figure 2D) and the collagen fibers were reduced in lungs of HEI3090-treated mice (Figure 2E, F).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Collagen fibers are reduced in lungs of HEI3090-treated mice.
source: We showed that both the percentage of CD140a (PDGFRα)-positive cells in non-immune cells subset (Figure 2D) and the collagen fibers were reduced in lungs of HEI3090-treated mice (Figure 2E, F).
evidence: The claim is supported by histological data shown in Figure 2E and 2F.

claim: HEI3090 inhibits the onset of lung fibrosis when administered during the inflammatory phase of the BLM model.
source: We also tested the ability of HEI3090 to limit lung fibrosis progression when administered during the inflammatory phase of the BLM model (Figure 2G) that mimics the exacerbation episodes in IPF patients (Peng et al., 2013). HEI3090 was also able to inhibit the onset of lung fibrosis in this setting given less damage on lung architecture (Figure 2H), the reduced fibrosis score (Figure 2I).
evidence: The claim is supported by histological data shown in Figure 2H and 2I.

claim: P2RX7 plays a role in the development of BLM-induced lung fibrosis.
source: In doing so, we initially observed that P2RX7 plays a role in the development of BLM-induced lung fibrosis. This is illustrated by a decrease of 50% in the Ashcroft score, with a mean value of 1.7 in P2RX7 knockout mice compared to 3 in WT mice (Figure 2M and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by data comparing P2RX7 knockout and WT mice shown in Figure 2M and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: HEI3090 failed to attenuate the remaining lung fibrosis in P2rx7−/− mice.
source: Additionally, in contrast to the observations in WT mice, HEI3090 failed to attenuate the remaining lung fibrosis in P2rx7−/− mice, as measured by the Ashcroft score (Figure 2M), the percentage of lung tissue with fibrotic lesions, or the intensity of collagen fibers (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2M and Figure 2—figure supplement 1D.

claim: HEI3090 exerts a specific antifibrotic effect through P2RX7.
source: These results show that P2RX7 alone participates in fibrosis and that HEI3090 exerts a specific antifibrotic effect through this receptor (see Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that HEI3090 does not work in P2RX7 knockout mice.

claim: Lung CD3+ T cells are more biased to produce IFN-γ than IL-17A when mice expressing P2RX7 are treated with HEI3090.
source: We show that lung CD3+ T cells were more biased to produce IFN-γ than the profibrotic IL-17A cytokine when mice expressing P2RX7 were treated with HEI3090 (Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: IL-17A production by Th17 cells is substantially attenuated after HEI3090 treatment.
source: Although levels of CD3+ T cells and T-cell subsets were unchanged (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D), including the profibrotic Th17 cells (Figure 3C), IL-17A production by Th17 cells is substantially attenuated after HEI3090 treatment (Figure 3C), consistent with the ability of IFN-γ to inhibit IL-17A production (Laurence et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Treatment with HEI3090 reduced TGFβ-producing immune cells in the lung.
source: Indeed, treatment with HEI3090 reduced TGFβ-producing immune cells in the lung as well as TGFβ production (Figure 3D).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: HEI3090 treatment reduced TGFβ production in NK cells but not in T-cell subsets.
source: Notably, HEI3090 treatment reduced TGFβ production in NK cells but not in T-cell subsets (Figure 3—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1F.

claim: In HEI3090-treated mice, the number of inflammatory monocytes decreased markedly.
source: We demonstrated that in HEI3090-treated mice, the number of inflammatory monocytes decreased markedly (Figure 3G), whereas the number of alveolar macrophages remained unchanged (Figure 3F), consistent with the prognostic ability of monocyte count in IPF progression (Achaiah et al., 2021; Kreuter et al., 2021; Liu et al., 2019; Scott et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3G.

claim: The number of alveolar macrophages remained unchanged in HEI3090-treated mice.
source: We demonstrated that in HEI3090-treated mice, the number of inflammatory monocytes decreased markedly (Figure 3G), whereas the number of alveolar macrophages remained unchanged (Figure 3F), consistent with the prognostic ability of monocyte count in IPF progression (Achaiah et al., 2021; Kreuter et al., 2021; Liu et al., 2019; Scott et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: Eosinophils are less present in HEI3090-treated lungs.
source: We also examined other inflammatory cells with profibrotic properties, such as eosinophils (Morimoto et al., 2018) that are less present in HEI3090-treated lungs (Figure 3G), or PMN levels that remain unchanged by HEI3090 treatment (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3G.

claim: PMN levels remain unchanged by HEI3090 treatment.
source: We also examined other inflammatory cells with profibrotic properties, such as eosinophils (Morimoto et al., 2018) that are less present in HEI3090-treated lungs (Figure 3G), or PMN levels that remain unchanged by HEI3090 treatment (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1D.

claim: HEI3090 promotes an antifibrotic cytokinic profile in lung immune cells.
source: Altogether these results demonstrate that HEI3090 promotes an antifibrotic cytokinic profile in lung immune cells and attenuates lung inflammation.
evidence: This is a summary statement based on the data presented in Figure 3.

claim: HEI3090 attenuates lung inflammation.
source: Altogether these results demonstrate that HEI3090 promotes an antifibrotic cytokinic profile in lung immune cells and attenuates lung inflammation.
evidence: This is a summary statement based on the data presented in Figure 3.

claim: Restriction of P2RX7 expression on immune cells restored the antifibrotic effect of HEI3090.
source: We show that restriction of P2RX7 expression on immune cells restored the antifibrotic effect of HEI3090 based on the architecture of the lung, with lungs of HEI3090-treated mice showing more free airspace and thinner alveolar walls (Figure 4B), as well as an overall lower fibrosis score (Figure 4C) and collagen fiber intensity (Figure 4D) than control lungs.
evidence: The claim is supported by adoptive transfer experiments shown in Figure 4B, 4C, and 4D.

claim: The absence of NLRP3 in P2RX7-expressing immune cells abrogated the ability of HEI3090 to inhibit lung fibrosis.
source: The absence of NLRP3 and IL-18 in P2RX7-expressing immune cells abrogated the ability of HEI3090 to inhibit lung fibrosis because the lung architecture and collagen fibers intensity resembled that of control mice (Figure 4E-J).
evidence: The claim is supported by adoptive transfer experiments shown in Figure 4E-J.

claim: The absence of IL-18 in P2RX7-expressing immune cells abrogated the ability of HEI3090 to inhibit lung fibrosis.
source: The absence of NLRP3 and IL-18 in P2RX7-expressing immune cells abrogated the ability of HEI3090 to inhibit lung fibrosis because the lung architecture and collagen fibers intensity resembled that of control mice (Figure 4E-J).
evidence: The claim is supported by adoptive transfer experiments shown in Figure 4E-J.

claim: Activation of P2RX7 with HEI3090 in WT mice increased the levels of IL-18 in the sera of these mice compared to control mice.
source: Consistent with the requirement of IL-18 for HEI3090's antifibrotic activity, activation of P2RX7 with this molecule in WT mice increased the levels of IL-18 in the sera of these mice compared to control mice (Figure 4K).
evidence: The claim is supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 4K.

claim: Neutralization of IL-18 abrogated the increase of the IFN-γ/IL-17A ratio by lung T cells.
source: Moreover, neutralization of IL-18 abrogated the increase of the IFN-γ/IL-17A ratio by lung T cells (Figure 4L), highlighting furthermore the necessity of IL-18 for the antifibrotic effect of HEI3090.
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4L.

claim: IL-1β was not involved in the antifibrotic effect of HEI3090.
source: However, IL-1β was not involved in the antifibrotic effect of HEI3090 (Figure 4—figure supplement 2C), nor were its levels affected by HEI3090 in WT mice (Figure 4—figure supplement 2D), in contrast to IL-18 levels measured in the same biological sample (Figure 4K).
evidence: The claim is supported by adoptive transfer experiments and ELISA data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2C and 2D.

claim: IL-1β levels were not affected by HEI3090 in WT mice.
source: However, IL-1β was not involved in the antifibrotic effect of HEI3090 (Figure 4—figure supplement 2C), nor were its levels affected by HEI3090 in WT mice (Figure 4—figure supplement 2D), in contrast to IL-18 levels measured in the same biological sample (Figure 4K).
evidence: The claim is supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2D.

claim: The P2RX7/NLRP3/IL-18 axis in immune cells is required to limit lung fibrosis progression.
source: Overall, we show that the P2RX7/NLRP3/IL-18 axis in immune cells is required to limit lung fibrosis progression, highlighting the efficacy in targeting the immune system in this disease.
evidence: This is a summary statement based on the data presented in Figure 4.

claim: The BLM lung fibrosis mouse model is the optimal model for studying IPF.
source: This lung fibrosis mouse model commonly employed in preclinical investigations, has recently been recognized as the optimal model for studying IPF (Jenkins et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Jenkins et al., 2017.

claim: Intrapulmonary administration of BLM induces DNA damage in alveolar epithelial type 1 cells.
source: In this model, the intrapulmonary administration of BLM induces DNA damage in alveolar epithelial type 1 cells, triggering cellular demise and the release of ATP.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about the BLM model.

claim: The extracellular release of ATP from injured cells activates the P2RX7/pannexin 1 axis, initiating the maturation of IL-1β and subsequent induction of inflammation and fibrosis.
source: The extracellular release of ATP from injured cells activates the P2RX7/pannexin 1 axis, initiating the maturation of IL-1β and subsequent induction of inflammation and fibrosis.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about the P2RX7/pannexin 1 axis.

claim: Mice lacking P2RX7 exhibited reduced neutrophil counts in their bronchoalveolar fluids and decreased levels of IL-1β in their lungs compared to WT mice.
source: In line with this, mice lacking P2RX7 exhibited reduced neutrophil counts in their bronchoalveolar fluids and decreased levels of IL-1β in their lungs compared to WT mice (Riteau et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Riteau et al., 2010.

claim: The transcriptional analysis indicated the downregulation of the P2RX7/IL-18/IFN-γ pathway in patients with IPF, where TGFβ levels are high.
source: The transcriptional analysis additionally indicated the downregulation of the P2RX7/IL-18/IFN-γ pathway in patients with IPF, where TGFβ levels are high (Khalil et al., 1991).
evidence: The claim is supported by transcriptomic analysis and a citation to Khalil et al., 1991.

claim: TGFβ downregulates IL-18R expression and IL-18-mediated IFN-γ production.
source: This is consistent with the ability of TGFβ to downregulate IL-18R expression and IL-18-mediated IFN-γ production (Koutoulaki et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Koutoulaki et al., 2010.

claim: P2RX7 is expressed by various immune and non-immune cells, but its expression is the highest in DCs and macrophages.
source: P2RX7 is expressed by various immune and non-immune cells, but its expression is the highest in DCs and macrophages (Di Virgilio and Vuerich, 2015), from which IL-18 is mainly released to shape the T-cell response (Sáez et al., 2017) and increase T-cell IFN-γ production (Iwai et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Di Virgilio and Vuerich, 2015.

claim: IL-18 is mainly released from DCs and macrophages to shape the T-cell response.
source: P2RX7 is expressed by various immune and non-immune cells, but its expression is the highest in DCs and macrophages (Di Virgilio and Vuerich, 2015), from which IL-18 is mainly released to shape the T-cell response (Sáez et al., 2017) and increase T-cell IFN-γ production (Iwai et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Sáez et al., 2017.

claim: IL-18 increases T-cell IFN-γ production.
source: P2RX7 is expressed by various immune and non-immune cells, but its expression is the highest in DCs and macrophages (Di Virgilio and Vuerich, 2015), from which IL-18 is mainly released to shape the T-cell response (Sáez et al., 2017) and increase T-cell IFN-γ production (Iwai et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Iwai et al., 2008.

claim: HEI3090 targets the P2RX7/IL-18 axis in DCs to shape the immune response in a lung tumor mouse model.
source: Accordingly, we have previously shown that HEI3090 targets the P2RX7/IL-18 axis in DCs to shape the immune response in a lung tumor mouse model (Douguet et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Douguet et al., 2021.

claim: HEI3090 needs ATP to potentiate P2RX7 and ATP is present only in injured tissues.
source: Noteworthy, in contrast to parenteral administration of IFN-γ which failed in clinical trial (King and Jobling, 2009), we did not observe any sign of systemic side effect likely because HEI3090 needs ATP to potentiate P2RX7 and ATP is present only in injured tissues.
evidence: This is based on the known mechanism of action of HEI3090 and the localization of ATP.

claim: IFN-γ suppresses IL-17A production.
source: It is not known whether this cytokinic and anti-inflammatory switch is solely due to the IL-17A and TGFβ-suppressive property of IFN-γ (de Bruin et al., 2010; Iwamoto et al., 1993; Penton-Rol et al., 1998), or whether it is a combination with the cell death-inducing property of P2RX7 (Surprenant et al., 1996).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to de Bruin et al., 2010; Iwamoto et al., 1993; Penton-Rol et al., 1998.

claim: IFN-γ suppresses TGFβ production.
source: It is not known whether this cytokinic and anti-inflammatory switch is solely due to the IL-17A and TGFβ-suppressive property of IFN-γ (de Bruin et al., 2010; Iwamoto et al., 1993; Penton-Rol et al., 1998), or whether it is a combination with the cell death-inducing property of P2RX7 (Surprenant et al., 1996).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to de Bruin et al., 2010; Iwamoto et al., 1993; Penton-Rol et al., 1998.

claim: P2RX7 has cell death-inducing properties.
source: It is not known whether this cytokinic and anti-inflammatory switch is solely due to the IL-17A and TGFβ-suppressive property of IFN-γ (de Bruin et al., 2010; Iwamoto et al., 1993; Penton-Rol et al., 1998), or whether it is a combination with the cell death-inducing property of P2RX7 (Surprenant et al., 1996).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Surprenant et al., 1996.

claim: HEI3090 failed to augment the release of IL-1β in the serum of mice treated with BLM, despite effectively increasing the release of IL-18.
source: However, in line with our prior in vivo and in vitro investigations (Douguet et al., 2021), HEI3090 failed to augment the release of IL-1β in the serum of mice treated with BLM, despite effectively increasing the release of IL-18.
evidence: The claim is supported by ELISA data and a citation to Douguet et al., 2021.

claim: ATP stimulation of alveolar macrophages, derived from both IPF and lung cancer patients, led exclusively to an elevation in IL-18 levels.
source: In agreement, previous reports have indicated that ATP stimulation of alveolar macrophages, derived from both IPF and lung cancer patients, led exclusively to an elevation in IL-18 levels (Lasithiotaki et al., 2018; Lasithiotaki et al., 2016), which was explained by an impaired NLRP3 inflammasome and a defective autophagy in IPF patients (Patel et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Lasithiotaki et al., 2018 and Lasithiotaki et al., 2016.

claim: An impaired NLRP3 inflammasome and a defective autophagy in IPF patients explains the exclusive elevation in IL-18 levels upon ATP stimulation.
source: In agreement, previous reports have indicated that ATP stimulation of alveolar macrophages, derived from both IPF and lung cancer patients, led exclusively to an elevation in IL-18 levels (Lasithiotaki et al., 2018; Lasithiotaki et al., 2016), which was explained by an impaired NLRP3 inflammasome and a defective autophagy in IPF patients (Patel et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Patel et al., 2012.

claim: Autophagy can be regulated by P2RX7.
source: Autophagy can be regulated by P2RX7 (de Bruin et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to de Bruin et al., 2010.

claim: Basal autophagy suppresses NLRP3-inflammasome activation and cytokine secretion.
source: Indeed, whereas basal autophagy suppresses NLRP3-inflammasome activation and cytokine secretion, induced autophagy augments IL-1β secretion (Dupont et al., 2011), therefore ruling out the hypothesis of HEI3090-induced autophagy to control the production of IL-1β.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Dupont et al., 2011.

claim: Induced autophagy augments IL-1β secretion.
source: Indeed, whereas basal autophagy suppresses NLRP3-inflammasome activation and cytokine secretion, induced autophagy augments IL-1β secretion (Dupont et al., 2011), therefore ruling out the hypothesis of HEI3090-induced autophagy to control the production of IL-1β.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Dupont et al., 2011.

claim: IL-18 is constitutively expressed in human and mouse immune cells.
source: Unlike IL-1β, IL-18 is constitutively expressed in human and mouse immune cells (Puren et al., 1999) but also in non-immune cells such as fibroblasts (Artlett et al., 2011) and lung epithelium (Watanabe et al., 2009) and is both matured and released after NLRP3 activation.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Puren et al., 1999.

claim: IL-18 is constitutively expressed in non-immune cells such as fibroblasts and lung epithelium.
source: Unlike IL-1β, IL-18 is constitutively expressed in human and mouse immune cells (Puren et al., 1999) but also in non-immune cells such as fibroblasts (Artlett et al., 2011) and lung epithelium (Watanabe et al., 2009) and is both matured and released after NLRP3 activation.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Artlett et al., 2011 and Watanabe et al., 2009.

claim: IL-18 is both matured and released after NLRP3 activation.
source: Unlike IL-1β, IL-18 is constitutively expressed in human and mouse immune cells (Puren et al., 1999) but also in non-immune cells such as fibroblasts (Artlett et al., 2011) and lung epithelium (Watanabe et al., 2009) and is both matured and released after NLRP3 activation.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about IL-18 processing.

claim: Clemastine enhances ATP-induced P2RX7-dependent Ca2+ entry, macropore opening and IL1B production in immune cells.
source: Clemastine, a first generation anti-histaminic, enhances ATP-induced P2RX7-dependent Ca2+ entry, macropore opening and IL1B production in immune cells (Nörenberg et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Nörenberg et al., 2011.

claim: When tested in vivo clemastine treatment does not activate P2RX7.
source: However, when tested in vivo clemastine treatment does not activates P2RX7, indeed it reduces the production of pro inflammatory cytokines and decreases P2RX7 expression in hippocampus (Su et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Su et al., 2018.

claim: Ginsenosides have been shown to potentiate ATP-induced P2RX7-dependent Ca2+ entry and macropore opening but also cell death in vitro.
source: Ginsenosides, purified from root of Panax ginseng, have been shown to potentiate ATP-induced P2RX7-dependent Ca2+ entry and macropore opening but also cell death in vitro (Helliwell et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Helliwell et al., 2015.

claim: There is no evidence indicating that ginsenosides act as positive modulators of P2RX7 in vivo.
source: So far, there is no evidence indicating that ginsenosides act as positive modulators of P2RX7 in vivo and all the other chemical compounds described to be active in vivo are negative allosteric modulator of P2RX7 (Karasawa and Kawate, 2016).
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge in the field.

claim: All the other chemical compounds described to be active in vivo are negative allosteric modulator of P2RX7.
source: So far, there is no evidence indicating that ginsenosides act as positive modulators of P2RX7 in vivo and all the other chemical compounds described to be active in vivo are negative allosteric modulator of P2RX7 (Karasawa and Kawate, 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Karasawa and Kawate, 2016.

claim: Therapies given to IPF patients are known to induce significant side effects which can limit their prescription.
source: Therapies given to IPF patients are known to induce significant side effects which can limit their prescription (Raghu et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Raghu et al., 2015.

claim: Several studies have indicated that P2RX7/NLRP3/IL-18 promote disease progression using knock out mice or inhibitors.
source: In this study, we emphasize the importance of IL-18 for an antifibrotic effect. Several studies have indicated that P2RX7/NLRP3/IL-18 promote disease progression using knock out mice or inhibitors (Artlett et al., 2011; Riteau et al., 2010; Zhang et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Artlett et al., 2011; Riteau et al., 2010; Zhang et al., 2019.

claim: Experimental mouse models rely on lung epithelial cell injury that has been shown to activate the NLRP3 inflammasome in the lung epithelium as a first step.
source: However, experimental mouse models rely on lung epithelial cell injury that has been shown to activate the NLRP3 inflammasome in the lung epithelium as a first step (Gasse et al., 2009; Riteau et al., 2010) and release danger signals that activate the immune system as a second step.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Gasse et al., 2009 and Riteau et al., 2010.

claim: NLRP3 and the release of IL-1β and IL-18 from fibroblasts have been shown to promote myofibroblast differentiation and extracellular matrix production.
source: In addition, NLRP3 and the release of IL-1β and IL-18 from fibroblasts have been shown to promote myofibroblast differentiation and extracellular matrix production (Artlett et al., 2011; Pinar et al., 2020; Watanabe et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Artlett et al., 2011; Pinar et al., 2020; Watanabe et al., 2009.

claim: IL-18 may have different effects depending on the cell type.
source: Since we have highlighted the importance of this pathway in immune cells for delaying fibrosis progression, we propose that IL-18 may have different effects depending on the cell type.
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed by the authors based on their findings.

claim: There is a lack of biomarkers for IPF, such as prognostic biomarkers, markers of disease activity, or markers of drug efficacy.
source: Beside an urgent need of new treatments for IPF, there is also a lack of biomarkers, such as prognostic biomarkers, markers of disease activity, or markers of drug efficacy.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of the field.

claim: Pirfenidone and nintedanib may affect IL-18 levels in preclinical models.
source: Given the potential effects of pirfenidone and nintedanib on IL-18 levels in preclinical models (Mavrogiannis et al., 2022; Oku et al., 2008; Sharawy and Serrya, 2020), determining IL-18 shifts during treatment would be highly interesting to evaluate potential changes in patients' outcome and to examine IL-18 levels which may be helpful in the long run for patient treatment strategy and subsequent introduction of pipeline drugs (Spagnolo et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Mavrogiannis et al., 2022; Oku et al., 2008; Sharawy and Serrya, 2020.

claim: HEI3090 acts selectively in an eATP-rich environment such as fibrotic lung.
source: Overall, we highlight in this study the ability of the P2RX7/NLRP3/IL-18 pathway in immune cells to inhibit the onset of lung fibrosis by using a positive modulator of P2RX7 that acts selectively in an eATP-rich environment such as fibrotic lung.
evidence: This is based on the known mechanism of action of HEI3090.

claim: HEI3090 enhances the antifibrotic properties of immune cells.
source: The unique feature of this strategy is that it enhances the antifibrotic and it attenuates the profibrotic properties of immune cells, with no reported side effects, at least in mice.
evidence: This is a summary statement based on the data presented in the manuscript.

claim: HEI3090 attenuates the profibrotic properties of immune cells.
source: The unique feature of this strategy is that it enhances the antifibrotic and it attenuates the profibrotic properties of immune cells, with no reported side effects, at least in mice.
evidence: This is a summary statement based on the data presented in the manuscript.

claim: No side effects of HEI3090 were reported, at least in mice.
source: The unique feature of this strategy is that it enhances the antifibrotic and it attenuates the profibrotic properties of immune cells, with no reported side effects, at least in mice.
evidence: This is based on the observations made during the experiments.
